title: Vibrant Shattering Japanese Pickle-Flavored Shallots Tonkotsu Ramen
description: A hearty, comforting bowl of Japanese-inspired ramen featuring vibrant, shattering shallots and the rich flavors of tonkotsu broth, all on a lazy Sunday afternoon.

ingredients.notes: Pork bones, chicken bones, and vegetables combined in a rich tonkotsu broth.

ingredients.name: Sliced Shallots
ingredients.notes: Thinly sliced and quickly pickled in a mixture of vinegar and sugar.

ingredients.name: Pork Belly
ingredients.notes: Braised in the tonkotsu broth until tender and flavorful.

ingredients.notes: Soft-boiled and sliced, adding creaminess and richness to the bowl.

ingredients.name: Green Onions
ingredients.notes: Thinly sliced and used as a garnish.

ingredients.name: Pickle Slices

ingredients.name: Sesame Seeds

instructions: Bring the tonkotsu broth to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.
In a separate pot of boiling water, cook the ramen noodles according to the package instructions.
In a small saucepan, combine the sliced shallots and vinegar, and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the shallots are caramelized and sticky.
In a large pan or Dutch oven, heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil over medium heat, then add the pork belly and cook until browned on all sides.
Add the sliced ginger and garlic to the pan and cook until fragrant.
Add the tonkotsu broth to the pan and bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the cooked ramen noodles to the pan and cook for an additional 2 minutes.
In a small bowl, beat the eggs and season with salt and black pepper.
Cook the eggs in a separate pot of boiling water until the whites are set and the yolks are cooked to your desired doneness.
Slice the cooked eggs and add them to the bowl.
Top the bowl with a portion of the cooked ramen noodles, a slice of the pickled shallots, a slice of the pork belly, and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.
Serve immediately and enjoy!
Remove the tonkotsu broth from the heat and let it cool slightly.
Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot, discarding the solids.
Bring the broth to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer and cook for an additional 5 minutes.
Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.
To make the pickled shallots, combine the sliced shallots and vinegar in a small bowl and let it sit at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Strain the pickled shallots through a fine-mesh sieve and discard the liquid.
Heat a small saucepan over medium heat, then add the vegetable oil and cook until hot.
Add the pork belly to the pan and cook until browned on all sides, then remove from heat and set aside.
Add the sliced ginger and garlic to the pan and cook until fragrant.
Add the tonkotsu broth to the pan and bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer and cook for an additional 10 minutes.
Add the cooked ramen noodles and cooked pork belly to the pan and cook for an additional 2 minutes.
Beat the eggs in a small bowl and season with salt and black pepper.
Cook the eggs in a separate pot of boiling water until the whites are set and the yolks are cooked to your desired doneness.
Slice the cooked eggs and add them to the bowl.
To make the tonkotsu broth, combine the pork bones, chicken bones, and vegetables in a large pot and add enough water to cover.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer and cook for 4 hours.
Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot, discarding the solids.
Add the sake, mirin, kombu, katsuobushi, and miso paste to the pot and bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer and cook for an additional 30 minutes.
Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.
